record.text: How do metabolites produced by the gut microbiota after bariatric surgery affect the host, according to EU-funded research?
record.reference_answer: Two projects trace a metabolite of the post-surgery gut microbiota to an effect on the host. EnteroBariatric reports that Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) shifts the microbiome from Firmicutes to the Proteobacteria phylum and raises faecal Enterobacteriaceae, and that metabolites of the RYGB-associated microbiota - notably tyramine, which can come directly from diet or be produced by intestinal Enterobacteriaceae and Enterococcaceae - promote colon cancer risk via increased DNA damage, cell proliferation and inflammation. Drug the bug runs the other way: the surgery-altered microbiota produces less imidazole propionate, a histidine-derived metabolite made by the microbial enzyme UrdA (urocanate reductase) that is elevated in prediabetes and type 2 diabetes and induces insulin resistance, so the project synthesized and screened more than 40 compounds seeking inhibitors of that enzyme as a new class of diabetes medication. The shared finding is that a molecule made by the reshaped gut community, rather than the weight loss itself, carries much of the surgery's systemic effect - lowering a pro-diabetic metabolite in one case, raising a pro-carcinogenic one in the other.
record.notes: Seeds from corpus_profile candidate vector-66 (bariatric surgery cluster, 4 projects corpus-wide); drift check re-ran the candidate SQL and reproduced 704779, 715662, 780659, 803526 exactly. A broader first wording ('what molecular mechanisms have projects identified by studying what changes after bariatric surgery') pooled 5 satisfying projects (715662, 780659, 803526, 695069, 694717) = L3, so the question was tightened to the microbiota-metabolite thread, which is where the two gold projects share a genuine common finding. Adjudications - IN: 715662 EnteroBariatric (RYGB-associated microbiota metabolites, tyramine, colon cancer risk), 780659 Drug the bug (imidazole propionate reduced after surgery, UrdA inhibitors). OUT: 803526 BARINAFLD (hybrid rank 7 - weight-loss-independent hepatic mechanisms, Egr1 and one-carbon/choline metabolism; no microbial metabolite); 695069 BYPASSWITHOUTSURGERY (gut hormone GLP-1 hypersecretion from host enteroendocrine cells, not microbial metabolites); 694717 ImmunoBile (bile acids and FXR/TGR5 immune signalling; its post-RYGB measurement is systemic total and conjugated bile-acid concentrations, host-conjugated, and it never links bacterial metabolite production to the surgery); 704779 Fit-The-Fat (VAT T cells, surgery only as background); 814638 GDS (non-surgical duodenal sleeve device, commercialization, no mechanism work); 633962 P4SB ('metabolic surgery' used metaphorically for engineering Pseudomonas putida); 796084 qMAR (antibiotic-resistance genes in paediatric transplant patients, not bariatric). evidence:
Gold 715662 EnteroBariatric - "Investigating Host-Microbial Interactions after Bariatric Surgery". Objective: "We, and others, have demonstrated that surgical interventions such as Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass (RYGB) modulates gut hormone levels, induces systemic metabolic changes and results in the shift of the microbiome from Firmicutes to the Proteobacteria phylum. ... My research programme aims to investigate the RYGB-specific gut microbiota impacts on host physiology and colon cancer risk." Report summary: "In addition to the clinical benefits of bariatric surgery, it results in altered urinary and faecal metabolic composition and an increase in the faecal abundance of Enterobacteriaceae bacterial family. ... The project findings indicated that metabolites produced by RYGB-associated gut microbiota modulate the colorectal cancer risk. For example, tyramine, which can directly come from diet or produced by intestinal Enterobacteriaceae and Enterococcaceae promotes colon cancer risk via increased DNA damage, cell proliferation, and inflammation." In associated projects we have demonstrated that imidazole propionate is associated with type 2 diabetes in humans and induce insulin resistance in primary hepatocytes and when injected into mice. Imidazole propionate is synthesized by the microbial enzyme UrdA from histidine. This POC will explore the potential of identifying inhibitors of UrdA to reduce production of imidazole propionate and thereby improve insulin sensitivity." Report summary: "...we recently identified a microbially produced metabolite from the amino acid histidine, imidazole propionate (ImP) to be elevated in patients with prediabetes and T2D. ... inhibition of the enzyme producing ImP, urocanate reductase, may be a plausible approach to treat T2D. ... we have synthesized and screened more than 40 compounds..."

record.reference_answer: Two projects trace a metabolite of the post-surgery gut microbiota to an effect on the host. EnteroBariatric reports that Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) shifts the microbiome from Firmicutes to the Proteobacteria phylum and raises faecal Enterobacteriaceae, and that metabolites of the RYGB-associated microbiota - notably tyramine, which can come directly from diet or be produced by intestinal Enterobacteriaceae and Enterococcaceae - promote colon cancer risk via increased DNA damage, cell proliferation and inflammation. Drug the bug runs the other way: the surgery-altered microbiota produces less imidazole propionate, a histidine-derived metabolite made by the microbial enzyme UrdA (urocanate reductase) that is elevated in prediabetes and type 2 diabetes and induces insulin resistance, so the project synthesized and screened more than 40 compounds seeking inhibitors of that enzyme as a new class of diabetes medication. The shared finding is that a molecule made by the reshaped gut community, rather than the weight loss itself, carries much of the surgery's systemic effect - lowering a pro-diabetic metabolite in one case, raising a pro-carcinogenic one in the other.

record.text: Which projects are engineering CAR T cells to attack solid tumours?
record.reference_answer: Eight H2020 projects engineer chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells against solid tumours, the setting where CAR therapy has lagged behind its success in blood cancers. Several build new CAR specificities: AngioCAR aims CAR T cells at extracellular vimentin (eVim) on the tumour vasculature, SweetCAR at sialic-acid carbohydrate neoantigens on carcinomas, and CARsen at senescent cells in solid tumours and senescence-associated disease. Others attack the hostile tumour microenvironment instead - Exh-Res-CART and Tex-Mex both work on T-cell exhaustion (biochemical and biomechanical triggers respectively), TRAP-CART uses gene-modified blood-derived cells in the tumour microenvironment to switch on programmable CAR T cells locally, with melanoma as its model cancer, and EnhancemenT modulates ZFP36/ZFP36L1 RNA-binding proteins in CAR-T cells to raise their in-vivo solid tumour-fighting capacity. CARAT is the platform case: automated GMP-compliant manufacture of CAR-modified T cells together with innovative CAR designs, intended to serve patients with incurable solid tumours as well as haematologic malignancies.

record.text: Which projects are engineering CAR T cells to attack solid tumours?
record.reference_answer: Eight H2020 projects engineer chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells against solid tumours, the setting where CAR therapy has lagged behind its success in blood cancers. Several build new CAR specificities: AngioCAR aims CAR T cells at extracellular vimentin (eVim) on the tumour vasculature, SweetCAR at sialic-acid carbohydrate neoantigens on carcinomas, and CARsen at senescent cells in solid tumours and senescence-associated disease. Others attack the hostile tumour microenvironment instead - Exh-Res-CART and Tex-Mex both work on T-cell exhaustion (biochemical and biomechanical triggers respectively), TRAP-CART uses gene-modified blood-derived cells in the tumour microenvironment to switch on programmable CAR T cells locally, with melanoma as its model cancer, and EnhancemenT modulates ZFP36/ZFP36L1 RNA-binding proteins in CAR-T cells to raise their in-vivo solid tumour-fighting capacity. CARAT is the platform case: automated GMP-compliant manufacture of CAR-modified T cells together with innovative CAR designs, intended to serve patients with incurable solid tumours as well as haematologic malignancies.

record.text: How do metabolites produced by the gut microbiota after bariatric surgery affect the host, according to EU-funded research?
record.reference_answer: Two projects trace a metabolite of the post-surgery gut microbiota to an effect on the host. EnteroBariatric reports that Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) shifts the microbiome from Firmicutes to the Proteobacteria phylum and raises faecal Enterobacteriaceae, and that metabolites of the RYGB-associated microbiota - notably tyramine, which can come directly from diet or be produced by intestinal Enterobacteriaceae and Enterococcaceae - promote colon cancer risk via increased DNA damage, cell proliferation and inflammation. Drug the bug runs the other way: the surgery-altered microbiota produces less imidazole propionate, a histidine-derived metabolite made by the microbial enzyme UrdA (urocanate reductase) that is elevated in prediabetes and type 2 diabetes and induces insulin resistance, so the project synthesized and screened more than 40 compounds seeking inhibitors of that enzyme as a new class of diabetes medication. In both, a molecule produced by the post-surgery gut microbiota is the proposed mediator of a host outcome: in Drug the bug the altered microbiota may be directly linked to some of the metabolic improvements observed following surgery, with imidazole propionate reduced after surgery, while in EnteroBariatric metabolites produced by RYGB-associated gut microbiota modulate the colorectal cancer risk.
